intro: Iran is a high plateau ringed by mountains, with two great deserts at its centre and seas to the north and south.

chapters.title: Mountains and plateau
text: The Zagros mountains run down the west and the Alborz along the north. Mount Damavand, a dormant volcano, is the highest peak in the Middle East at about 5,600 m.
Most of Iran sits on a plateau over 1,000 m high, and much of the population lives in the mountain foothills.

chapters.title: Deserts
text: The Dasht-e Kavir (salt desert) and Dasht-e Lut fill the centre. Satellites have measured some of the hottest ground temperatures on Earth in the Lut desert, over 70 °C.
Ancient underground canals called qanats carry water from mountains to towns and farms.

chapters.title: Two seas
text: The Caspian coast in the north is green, rainy and covered in forest. In the south, the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz carry a large share of the world's oil.
